questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: namespace-scoped configs, Secrets, ConfigMaps, PVCs, InitContainers, Probes, and NetworkPolicies in a real-ops pattern.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped CronJob
- ConfigMap for policy definitions
- Secret for API token
- ConfigMap for status persistence
- PersistentVolumeClaim for logs
- InitContainer for tooling
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress to policy portal

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob skeleton (placeholders:
# namespace: <target-namespace>, policy-config: <ConfigMap>, logs-pvc: <PVC>)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-policy-guardian
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "0,30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: fetch-tools
              image: appropriate/curl-jq
              command: ["sh","-c","echo init"]
          containers:
            - name: guardian
              image: <registry>/image-policy-guardian:latest
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: <logs-pvc>
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test failure modes (policy update, portal unreachable, token expiry)?
- What are the performance and RBAC trade-offs of namespace-scoped policies vs cluster-wide controllers?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: reading from a PVC, using ConfigMaps/Secrets, InitContainers, sidecars, probes, and a NetworkPolicy in a real self-healing workflow.

## Key Concepts
- PVC-mounted config and health specs
- ConfigMap-based knobs (BATCH_SIZE)
- Deployment lifecycle and rollout restart trigger
- InitContainer and TLS sidecar usage
- Readiness/Liveness probes and security network policy

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for the healer deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: healer
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: healer
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: health-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: health
          mountPath: /health
      containers:
      - name: healer-core
        image: your-registry/healer:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: health
          mountPath: /health
        readinessProbe:

            path: /health/ready
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/live
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: health
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: health-pvc
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: reg-cred
```

## Why This Is Asked

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-refresh
  namespace: ckad
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fetch-secrets

          mountPath: /vault/secrets
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: vault
          mountPath: /vault/secrets
      volumes:
      - name: vault
        emptyDir: {}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests comprehensive CKAD skills including per-namespace isolation, configuration management with ConfigMaps and Secrets, InitContainers for dependency setup, sidecar patterns for auxiliary services, health probes for reliability, RBAC for security, and NetworkPolicy for traffic control.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers for runtime dependency installation
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for configuration and credential management
- Sidecar containers for TLS certificate rotation
- Readiness and liveness probes for health monitoring
- Namespace isolation and NetworkPolicy for security boundaries
- Dead-letter queue implementation on PVC storage
- At-least-once delivery semantics with batch processing

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ns-collector
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: install-deps
    image: alpine:latest
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache nats-cli']
  containers:
  - name: collector
    image: collector:latest
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: ns-collector-config
    - secretRef:
        name: ns-collector-creds
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
    volumeMounts:
    - name: dlq-pvc
      mountPath: /dlq
  - name: tls-sidecar
    image: tls-sidecar:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls-certs
      mountPath: /etc/tls
  volumes:
  - name: dlq-pvc
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: dlq-pvc
  - name: tls-certs
    secret:
      secretName: tls-certs
```

## Trade-offs
- **At-least-once vs exactly-once**: At-least-once provides simpler implementation but may cause duplicate processing
- **Sidecar overhead**: TLS rotation adds resource consumption but improves security
- **PVC vs temporary storage**: PVC provides persistence but increases complexity and cost
- **NetworkPolicy restrictions**: Improve security but may impact debugging and monitoring capabilities

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1

metadata:
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: CronJob usage with Kaniko, PVC-backed build context, ConfigMap-driven config, rollout triggers via checksum, resource budgeting, and health checks. It also covers RBAC, network isolation, and upgrade/downgrade workflows.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob with Kubernetes Jobs and Kaniko
- ConfigMap mounting and rollout triggers via PodTemplate checksum annotation
- Resource requests/limits
- Readiness/Liveness probes and startup behavior
- preStop lifecycle hook
- PodDisruptionBudget
- RBAC: Role/RoleBinding for build operations
- NetworkPolicy isolation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Skeleton: CronJob with Kaniko build from PVC, mounts ConfigMap, and RBAC
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-build
  namespace: ci
spec:
  schedule: "*/15 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: kaniko-builder
          containers:
          - name: kaniko
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to compose CKAD primitives into a small, observable application with proper security and observability patterns.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for configuration management
- InitContainers and Sidecars for application lifecycle management
- Probes (readiness and liveness) for health monitoring
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for traffic security
- RBAC basics for in-namespace metrics access
- Observability and security trade-offs in containerized applications

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment sketch
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: python-api
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: python-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: python-api
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-deps
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'pip install -r /app/requirements.txt']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['python', '/app/main.py']
        env:
        - name: ENABLE_METRICS
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: app-config
              key: ENABLE_METRICS
        - name: API_USERNAME
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: username
        - name: API_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: password
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      - name: cert-rotator
        image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /etc/certs
      volumes:
      - name: app-code
        configMap:
          name: app-code
      - name: certs
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: monitoring
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9000
```

## Trade-offs
- **Security vs. Complexity**: NetworkPolicy adds security but increases deployment complexity
- **Resource Overhead**: Sidecar containers double resource requirements for cert management
- **Observability Cost**: Metrics endpoint requires additional monitoring infrastructure
- **InitContainer Impact**: Dependency installation extends pod startup time
- **Namespace Isolation**: Per-namespace design improves security boundaries but requires duplicate configuration management

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design per-namespace automation with auditability and tight network controls. Image provenance is a critical security concern for multi-tenant environments like Discord or Airbnb, where ensuring container images come from trusted registries is essential.

## Key Concepts
- **CKAD Scheduling**: CronJob for recurring audit tasks
- **Image Provenance**: Registry API integration, image digests (SHA256)
- **Secrets & ConfigMaps**: REGISTRY_TOKEN for authentication, audit-status for state tracking
- **PV-backed Storage**: PVC at /audit for persistent digest reports
- **InitContainers**: Installing required tools (curl, jq) for image inspection
- **Readiness Probes**: Ensuring the pod is ready before accepting traffic
- **Namespace NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress to only trusted registries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-audit
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: audit-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
          containers:
          - name: auditor
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "..."]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
            - name: registry-token
              mountPath: /secrets
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "[ -f /audit/ready ]"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
          volumes:
          - name: audit-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: audit-pvc
          - name: registry-token
            secret:
              secretName: REGISTRY_TOKEN
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-status
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  last_run: ""
  digest_count: "0"
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: registry-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: registry
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **CronJob vs Job**: CronJob provides scheduling but has slight timing drift; use precise timing if required.
- **PVC Size**: Allocate sufficient storage based on pod count and audit frequency.
- **InitContainer Overhead**: Adds startup time but ensures tools are available; consider using a custom image with pre-installed tools.
- **NetworkPolicy Scope**: A permissive egress may be necessary if multiple registries are used; balance security with operational flexibility.
- **ConfigMap Updates**: Frequent updates may cause contention; consider annotation-based status or external database for high-frequency audits.

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical CKAD-level skills in CronJobs, Secrets, ConfigMaps, and job lifecycle management, including verification and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job resources using the batch/v1 API
- ConfigMap volume mounts for configuration and script files
- Secret injection as environment variables
- CronJob policies: concurrencyPolicy, backoffLimit, and successfulJobsHistoryLimit

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backfill
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  backoffLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: db-backfill
            image: postgres:15-alpine
            env:
            - name: PGHOST
              value: db.analytics.svc.cluster.local
            - name: PGPORT
              value: "5432"
            - name: PGUSER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: username
            - name: PGPASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: password
            command:
            - psql
            - -f
            - /scripts/backfill.sql
            volumeMounts:
            - name: scripts
              mountPath: /scripts
          volumes:
          - name: scripts
            configMap:
              name: backfill-scripts
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Verification Steps
1. Apply the manifest: `kubectl apply -f db-backfill-cronjob.yaml`
2. Verify creation: `kubectl get cronjob db-backfill -n analytics`
3. Check resource details: `kubectl describe cronjob db-backfill -n analytics`
4. View scheduled jobs: `kubectl get jobs -n analytics --watch`
5. Inspect pod logs: `kubectl logs <pod-name> -n analytics`

## Rollback Steps
1. Immediate: `kubectl delete cronjob db-backfill -n analytics`
2. Restore previous version: `kubectl apply -f db-backfill-cronjob.yaml.backup`
3. Suspend job temporarily: `kubectl patch cronjob db-backfill -n analytics -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`

```yaml
# LimitRange
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
---
# ResourceQuota
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: resource-quota
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "10"
    requests.cpu: "1"
    requests.memory: 1Gi
    limits.cpu: "2"
    limits.memory: 2Gi
---
# Deployment (inherits defaults)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-app
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Trade-offs
**Advantages:**
- Prevents resource starvation across namespaces
- Enforces fair resource distribution
- Automatic defaults reduce configuration errors
- Provides cost control boundaries

**Considerations:**
- Too restrictive limits can hinder scaling
- Default limits may be overprovisioned for small workloads
- ResourceQuota refusals require manual quota increases
- May impact autoscaling behavior if quotas are too tight

**Best Practices:**
- Set conservative defaults but allow overrides
- Monitor quota utilization regularly
- Use separate quotas for production vs development
- Consider pod priority classes for critical workloads

```yaml
        runAsNonRoot: true
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a practical, namespace-scoped canary upgrade using standard CKAD tools: CronJob scheduling, patching Deployments, ConfigMaps/Secrets for config and credentials, and PVC-based logging. It also exercises InitContainers, probes, and network policy considerations in a real workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and JobTemplate execution
- Patching Deployment images with kubectl set image or patch
- Reading image tag from ConfigMap and registry authentication via Secret
- Persisting status in a ConfigMap and logging to a PVC
- InitContainer to install tooling (kubectl, jq)
- Readiness/Liveness probes for the Job Pod
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting registry egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-upgrade
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq; true"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          containers:
          - name: upgrader
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "set -e; CANARY_TAG=$(kubectl get configmap canary-config -o jsonpath='{.data.tag}'); kubectl patch deployment my-app -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"my-app","image":"myrepo/my-app:${CANARY_TAG}"}]}}}}' --record; echo done; sleep 1"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement idempotent patches and roll back on failure?
- How to measure canary success (latency, error rate) before full rollout?
- How would this scale across many namespaces or deployments?

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-validator
spec:
  schedule: "*/3 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:

      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: config-validator-sa

                claimName: manifests-pvc
```
